messages.author: cd9baedf48d871eb
messages.subject: geom_point and pdf readers other than adobe
parts:
Hi,

Does anyone use ggplot2 to output pdf files and then read them with
readers that are not adobe's?

I use okular under linux and sumatrapdf under windows. I have trouble
with geom_point. While it works fine with adobe reader, with these
other readers I don't see points, but other symbols (a "q" with okular
and a "1" with sumatra").
I tried to manually set the shape, but shapes 16, 19, 20 or 21 all
give the same results.
However, when I increase the size of the points (a lot), it becomes
all right.

I guess that a real circle is drawn for big sizes, and for small ones
a character is used. Then, alternative readers would not read this
character properly. Does that make sense and is there a workaround?

Thanks,

Xavier

This is indeed what happens. I have seen it when importing the PDFs in
Inkscape. The culprit is the pdf device of R. I have found that
producing PDFs with the cairo device (I think it is installed by
default on recent R versions on Linux) solves the issue.
install.packages("Cairo")
library("Cairo")
CairoPDF()

Let me know if that works. I haven't worked on Linux for a while (and
producing PDFs via the quartz device on OS X does not show the
problem).

JiHO

messages.author: 5ec5102a43e29af7
messages.subject: Re: geom_point and pdf readers other than adobe
parts:
maybe your system is missing some fonts.

When I plot this:

ggplot(mtcars)+geom_point(aes(pmg,cyl))

and export the plot to a pdf file, okular tells me it uses the following
fonts (pdf properties dialog):

- Helvetica /usr/share/font/type1/gsfonts/n019003l.pfb
- ZapfDingbats /usr/share/font/type1/gsfonts/d050000l.pfb

The one responsible for the points should be ZapfDingbats, which are
part of the gsfonts package (in ubuntu).


If it is a font problem, you can also define the fonts yourself with the
parameter font:

fonts: a character vector specifying R graphics font family names
for fonts which will be included in the PDF file. Defaults
to 'NULL'.

or try this option:

useDingbats: logical. Should small circles be rendered _via_ the
Dingbats font? Defaults to 'TRUE', which produces smaller
and better output. Setting this to 'FALSE' can
work around font display problems in broken PDF viewers. See
the 'Note' for a possible fix for such viewers.

see ?pdf


regards,
stefan
